description: Two concurrent claimLease calls for one claimable job produce exactly one lease and one no-work result.
No interleaving may leave two open leases for the same job and collection cycle.
Submission, extension, and abandonment by a worker other than the lease holder are refused without disclosing lease state.
Concurrent submissions with the same lease, input hash, and result hash yield one acceptance and byte-identical replays.
A different input or result hash for a lease with an accepted row conflicts and cannot overwrite that row.
Lease expiry and same-cycle requeue are one transaction with no observable expired-but-not-requeued interval.
A result-level requeue terminalizes the old cycle and creates exactly one next cycle atomically.
The new collection cycle, current permit epoch, and recomputed input hash become visible together or not at all.
Replica listing for a new collection cycle never returns accepted evidence from an earlier cycle.
Concurrent authorization calls sharing an effect intent ID create one identity; exact inputs replay and different inputs conflict.
Concurrent verdicts for one adjudication request persist at most one canonical verdict and one terminal transition.
Concurrent reserve charges with the same charge key consume capacity exactly once.
Two authorizations racing for a lane's final unit yield one authorized and charged result plus one escalation-budget denial, never overdraw or uncharged authorization.
Invalidating an epoch in one class never selects a second class that reuses the same epoch label.
A multi-cycle invalidation applies every expected target and distinct requeue plan in one transaction or changes nothing.
A target created or transitioned after scope inspection makes compare-and-apply invalidation conflict without partial mutation.
Emergency withdrawal publishes the new current epoch together with every invalidation and requeue, never before or after.
Suspension or revocation and closure/requeue of every holder lease are one atomic worker-state command.
Concurrent class-version registrations replay identical schema hashes and conflict on different hashes without replacement.
Concurrent adjudication reads retain the persisted openedAt used for starvation dwell calculations.
Concurrent reputation records with one evidence ID persist one canonical record; exact records replay and changed records conflict.
Two prepared leases comparing against one candidate revision produce one winner; Store never selects or ranks the candidate.
A newly accepted replica or open lease makes the expected worker-exclusion snapshot stale and refuses claim.
A result requeue that advances collectionCycle invalidates every candidate snapshot from the old cycle.
A queue-mode or class-health revision change between candidate read and compare-and-claim refuses the prepared lease.
Concurrent prepared claims from one worker compare the same contribution revision and cannot exceed the declared cap.
A prepared claim bound to an earlier assigned-slot occurrence conflicts after the durable occurrence advances.
A prepared domain command using an already-durable IdSource identity conflicts and never replaces the existing record.
An IdSource lease ID consumed by a losing stale-snapshot claim may be skipped but leaves no durable lease or alias.
Emergency halt racing enqueue makes either the enqueue visible before the complete halt snapshot or refuses it; no work enters through a half-visible halt.
Emergency halt racing compare-and-claim makes either the lease visible before the complete halt snapshot or refuses it; no lease crosses the halt revision.
An automatic class-health refresh comparing an old revision conflicts after an operator emergency halt.
Queue mode, affected class-health revisions, invalidations, and authorization validity changes become visible in one precedence-consistent transaction.
A charge carrying an old reserve policy version or rollover identity conflicts without consuming either old or current capacity.
Concurrent registration of one worker persists the immutable worker and initial routing record together; identical input replays and changed input conflicts.
Two routing-period transitions comparing one revision produce one winner while preserving the Store-owned open-lease set.
Concurrent class-health initialization creates one snapshot; identical input replays and a different initial value conflicts without replacement.
